source_snapshot.procedure: Enter BIOS with no password, set an Administrator password within the defined range, save/reset, make exactly three wrong-password attempts, enter with the correct password, clear it by submitting an empty new password, save/reset and verify passwordless BIOS entry.
source_snapshot.criteria: Verify passwordless baseline, supported password creation, rejection of wrong passwords, correct-password entry and successful clearing.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek correctly identifies a manual BIOS UI test and lockout risk but only summarizes set/reboot/prompt behavior and does not preserve the full three-wrong-attempt, correct-entry and clear-to-baseline sequence.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify the complete BIOS Administrator Password lifecycle: passwordless entry, valid temporary-password creation, rejection of exactly three wrong attempts, acceptance of the correct password after reset, clearing, and restored passwordless entry.
original_test_intent.target: The Administrator Password control and BIOS-entry authentication path on the exact SUT/BIOS build, operated through an approved pre-OS console.
original_test_intent.scope: One ordered set/save/reset/three-negative-attempt/correct-entry/clear/save/reset/final-entry sequence using a non-production temporary secret that satisfies the documented platform rules.
original_test_intent.operation: Confirm the passwordless baseline and recovery readiness, create the approved temporary secret without exposing it, save/reset, attempt exactly three pre-authorized wrong values without exceeding the platform-safe boundary, authenticate with the correct secret, clear using the documented empty-password method, save/reset and prove passwordless BIOS entry plus normal boot/management health.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One lifecycle sequence; exactly three wrong-password attempts as specified, with two save/reset transitions. The 15-minute fields are estimates, not a shortened substitute for any step.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The BIOS accepts an in-range supported temporary password, rejects all three wrong attempts without an unexpected unrecoverable lockout, accepts the correct password, clears the Administrator Password, and subsequently permits passwordless BIOS entry with normal platform health.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/BIOS identity, approved password-rule and retry/lockout references, passwordless baseline, authorization/recovery readiness, redacted timestamps and results for set/save/reset, each of three wrong attempts, correct entry, clear/save/reset and final passwordless entry, plus final boot/OOB health. No secret content.
ambiguities: The allowed length/character range, retry/lockout behavior and recovery method are not stated.
The blank-new-password clear mechanism and prompt flow must be confirmed for the exact BIOS build.
The source does not specify local versus approved remote console; either must protect secret entry and provide reliable pre-OS interaction.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 accurately restores the entire source sequence, keeps password entry manual, defines exactly three wrong attempts, protects the secret, requires owner rules/recovery and proves final passwordless restoration. No material technical or safety correction is required.

applicable_history.decision: The historical review identifies a human BIOS-console operation and lockout risk; V2 already corrects its missing lifecycle and evidence detail.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep V2's classification and safeguards. This is an ordered security-state lifecycle requiring human secret entry and visual authentication judgment; absent password/lockout/recovery rules delay execution but do not make the purpose semantically BLOCKED.

available_now: The source defines the complete state sequence and exact wrong-attempt count.
Read-only SUT/BIOS/OOB inventory and recovery-path checks can be prepared without touching the password state.
V2 already requires secret redaction and final baseline restoration.
missing_inputs: Exact supported Administrator Password length/characters and platform-specific empty-password clearing procedure
Documented behavior after the first, second and third wrong attempts, any delay/lockout threshold and owner-approved recovery procedure
Secure temporary-secret custody, approved console/operator, maintenance window and OOB access
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The BIOS/security owner supplies the password and lockout/clear specifications and controls the temporary secret; the lab/system owner supplies the approved console, maintenance window and proven recovery path.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect SUT, board and BIOS build plus BMC/OOB reachability and normal boot health without clearing logs
Review the exact BIOS security-page procedure and prepare redacted evidence checkpoints that record outcomes but never keystrokes or secret values
prohibited_until_closed: Do not set, guess, transmit, print, record in screenshots or log any credential; do not begin wrong attempts without the exact retry/lockout policy and recovery readiness
Do not exceed three wrong attempts, improvise a clear/reset method, use a production/reused secret, release the SUT with a password set or perform an unapproved CMOS/NVRAM recovery
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The exact BIOS build's password, lockout and clear rules are signed off; the temporary secret is held in an approved secret channel; console/window/OOB recovery are tested; the operator can execute all eight source steps and prove final passwordless state without exposing the secret.

revision_candidate.purpose: Verify creation, negative authentication, correct authentication and clearing of the BIOS Administrator Password, ending at the original passwordless state.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact SUT and BIOS build in an approved maintenance window with a secure local or remote pre-OS console, documented security rules and working BMC/OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Only the BIOS Administrator Password control and BIOS-entry authentication flow; exactly three wrong attempts and two required save/reset cycles, with no OS or BMC credential changes.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Password length/character rules; retry/lockout behavior; documented blank-password clear flow; approved non-production temporary secret held securely; console/operator/window; OOB/vendor recovery and final-state checklist.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Verify passwordless BIOS entry; set the approved temporary Administrator Password; save/reset; record the rejection outcome of exactly three wrong attempts; authenticate with the correct password; clear it through the documented empty-new-password flow; save/reset; verify passwordless BIOS entry and normal system health.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct SUT/BIOS and passwordless baseline verified; security owner approval; secret custody and redacted capture configured; retry/lockout/clear rules known; console and OOB recovery tested; maintenance window active; logs preserved.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Build/rule/approval and baseline identifiers; redacted outcome and timestamp for password set, each reset, each of three wrong attempts, correct entry and clear; final passwordless entry plus normal boot/OOB health; no password value or keystroke capture.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform BIOS security specification for supported password syntax, retry/lockout and clear behavior, together with the eight-step source procedure.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never expose or reuse the temporary secret, exceed three wrong attempts, continue after unexpected lockout, improvise firmware/NVRAM recovery, omit final clearing or treat a saved password as an acceptable final state.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: The BIOS/security owner approves the temporary-secret process, negative attempts, resets and recovery. A human operator performs secret entry and judges prompts; the owner accepts final redacted evidence.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: All BIOS password entry, prompt interpretation and security-state changes are manual. An agent may coordinate non-secret checkpoints and read-only health evidence but must never receive or enter the password.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On unexpected lockout, correct-secret rejection, clear failure or boot/management loss, stop all guesses, preserve redacted state, invoke only the approved owner/vendor recovery procedure, re-establish the passwordless baseline and verify health before any retry.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unknown rules or baseline, missing approval/secret custody/console/OOB recovery, unexpected prompt or lockout, any secret exposure, correct-password rejection, clear/save/reset failure, fourth wrong attempt, or inability to prove final passwordless and healthy state.

identified_defects: DeepSeek omits most of the required lifecycle and suggests credentials be recorded, which is unsafe if interpreted as recording the secret.
The source omits platform-specific password, lockout, clear and recovery rules.
reason_for_change: No material V2 change is warranted: its scope, classification, security handling, exact attempt boundary and recovery controls already preserve the source and address the identified defects.
removed_ambiguities: V2 already makes the three-attempt boundary, secure secret handling and final passwordless restoration explicit.
resolved_blockers: The intent is clear and manual execution is feasible once owner-supplied rules and approvals are available; their absence is execution readiness, not a permanent BLOCKED classification.
remaining_blockers: Do not begin until password syntax, three-attempt safety, clear method, secure secret custody, approval and proven recovery are all available.
objective_improvement_over_v2: None required; KEEP is objectively correct because V2 already fixes DeepSeek's incomplete lifecycle, secret-handling and lockout/recovery defects without changing the eight-step source intent.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The isolated validator preserved the ordered administrator-password lifecycle, exactly three rejected attempts, two save/reset cycles, secret protection and final passwordless state.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 uniquely retains all three authentication stages, exact wrong-attempt count, secret redaction and return to passwordless baseline.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Keep secrets outside evidence, stop at any unexpected lockout, never exceed three wrong attempts, and require an owner-controlled recovery path plus final cleared-state proof.
